backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to the current 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold it at 0.95. Implement by computing the momentum value each step from the step counter and writing it into the Muon param-group dict before the update. No other changes.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from 5 to 3. This cuts optimizer overhead so more steps fit in the 300 s budget. Keep the same quintic coefficients and the same normalization, and change only the iteration count constant.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon

backlog.spec: Replace the Muon per-matrix LR scale factor sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) with a match-RMS scale of 0.2*sqrt(max(rows, cols)) applied to the orthogonalized update. This lets the Muon matrices share a similar effective LR with the Adam-trained parameters. Retune MATRIX_LR is not needed for the first test, so keep MATRIX_LR at 0.04 and adjust only the scale expression.
backlog.title: Shape-matched RMS scaling for Muon updates

backlog.spec: Change the AdamW betas for embeddings, lm_head and per-layer scalars from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.8, 0.99) and set the Adam epsilon from 1e-8 to 1e-10. Leave Muon and all other settings unchanged. This makes the second-moment estimate smoother over the short run.
backlog.title: Higher Adam beta2 and smaller epsilon for non-Muon params

backlog.spec: Scale the Muon weight decay (currently 0.2) by a factor that decreases linearly from 1.0 at the start of training to 0.0 at the end, computed from elapsed time over the time budget. Apply the factor each step to the decay term only. This keeps regularization strong early and lets the final weights fit the data.
backlog.title: Linearly decayed weight decay

backlog.spec: Increase UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008 while leaving every other hyperparameter unchanged. The lm_head is the only output projection, so a larger rate may speed convergence of the output distribution within the short run.
backlog.title: Raise lm_head Adam learning rate

backlog.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate decays over the final 70 percent of the time budget instead of the final 50 percent. Keep the linear shape and all other settings as they are.
backlog.title: Longer warmdown phase

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown multiplier with a cosine decay: multiplier = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)) where p is the fraction of the warmdown window elapsed, applied to all parameter groups. The warmdown still starts at (1-WARMDOWN_RATIO) of the time budget and ends at zero LR.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown shape

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.02 and use a linear ramp from 0 to 1 over the first 2 percent of the time budget for all parameter groups. This avoids a large initial update when Muon and high-LR Adam groups start, while still leaving most of the budget at full LR.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.1 so the learning rate floors at 10 percent of its initial value at the end of the warmdown instead of reaching zero. Keep the linear warmdown shape and all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Non-zero final learning rate

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 with the schedule unchanged. The Muon-trained matrices are the bulk of the parameters, and a higher peak may reach a lower loss within the fixed 300 s budget if the warmdown remains stable.
backlog.title: Higher Muon peak learning rate

backlog.spec: Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 and keep all other values fixed. The current embedding LR is very aggressive for Adam, so this checks whether a smaller rate reduces noise in the token embeddings and improves validation bits per byte.
backlog.title: Lower embedding learning rate

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so each optimizer step covers about 262K tokens. Keep the learning rates the same. This doubles the number of optimizer steps in the fixed wall-clock budget, which may help more than the reduced gradient quality.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch size

backlog.spec: Start with a total batch of 2**17 tokens and double it at 25 percent and 60 percent of the time budget up to 2**19, adjusting the gradient accumulation count at each change. Keep learning rates at their current values. Early small batches give more updates when the loss is highest.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp during training

backlog.spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a SwiGLU block: a gate and an up projection to hidden size round(8/3 * model_dim), then SiLU(gate) times up, then a down projection. Scale the hidden size so the total MLP parameter count matches the current model. Keep the attention and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: SwiGLU MLP at matched parameter count

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH from 8 to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48 so model_dim stays near 512 while adding two layers. Keep HEAD_DIM, learning rates and all other settings unchanged. This tests whether extra depth helps within the fixed time budget.
backlog.title: Deeper narrower model

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH from 8 to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 80 so model_dim grows to about 480 while the layer count drops. Keep HEAD_DIM and all other settings unchanged. This tests whether a faster, wider model gets more progress per second.
backlog.title: Shallower wider model

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "LLLL" so every layer attends over the full context instead of using half-context sliding windows in three of four layers. Keep everything else unchanged. This tests whether the shorter windows are limiting quality at this sequence length.
backlog.title: Full attention in every layer

backlog.spec: Save the value projection output of the first attention layer and add a learned per-layer mixing of it into the value of each later attention layer, v_l = v_l + lambda_l * v_0, with lambda_l initialized to zero. Use one scalar per layer added to the existing scalar parameters. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: ResFormer-style value residual

backlog.spec: Raise the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000 so low-frequency rotary components cover longer distances. Keep all other settings unchanged. This is a single-constant change in the rotary embedding setup.
backlog.title: Larger RoPE base

backlog.spec: If the model applies a tanh logit softcap, change its cap from the current value to 30. If no softcap exists, add logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) before the cross-entropy. Keep the rest unchanged. This tests whether bounding the output logits helps training stability at the current learning rates.
backlog.title: Tighter logit softcap

backlog.spec: Use grouped-query attention with n_kv_head equal to half of n_head, so each key and value head is shared by two query heads. Keep the query head count and HEAD_DIM unchanged and reduce the k and v projection output size accordingly. This lowers attention parameter count and memory, which may allow more steps per second.
backlog.title: Grouped-query attention with two KV heads

backlog.spec: Add a z-loss term 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training cross-entropy loss, computed over all non-padding positions. Keep the evaluation path and all other settings unchanged. This discourages the output logit norm from drifting and can stabilize the high-LR output head.
backlog.title: Z-loss regularization on logits

backlog.spec: Exclude the token embedding and lm_head weights from the weight decay term, applying decay only to the Muon-trained matrices and the per-layer weights. Keep all learning rates unchanged. This avoids shrinking the embedding rows that have high LR and sparse gradients.
backlog.title: No weight decay on embeddings and lm_head

backlog.spec: Clip the global gradient norm of all trainable parameters to 1.0 before each optimizer step, computed after the backward pass and before the Muon and Adam updates. Keep everything else unchanged. This guards against the occasional large update that high LR can produce.
backlog.title: Global gradient norm clipping

backlog.spec: Train with a shorter sequence length of 512 tokens for the first 40 percent of the time budget and switch to the full sequence length afterwards, increasing the batch row count so tokens per step stay at TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE. Keep learning rates unchanged. Short sequences early give cheaper steps and more updates.
backlog.title: Progressive sequence length

backlog.spec: Halve the training sequence length and double the number of sequences per device batch so the total tokens per optimizer step stay the same. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE memory in check by using gradient accumulation if needed. Keep the model and learning rates unchanged. This tests whether shorter context windows with more examples improves the bits per byte within the budget.
backlog.title: Halved sequence length with doubled batch rows

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Right before the final evaluation call, copy the EMA weights into the model. Do not change the evaluation call or the summary printing. This smooths the final weights taken from the noisy late high-LR phase.
backlog.title: Exponential moving average of weights

backlog.spec: Enable fused=True for the AdamW optimizers and make sure Muon uses the foreach or batched path for its matrix updates, so optimizer steps launch fewer CUDA kernels. Keep the hyperparameters and update math unchanged. This increases throughput and therefore the number of training steps in the fixed 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Fused and foreach optimizer kernels

backlog.spec: Share one matrix between the token embedding and the lm_head. Initialize it with the embedding init, and remove the separate lm_head parameter group, so UNEMBEDDING_LR no longer applies. Keep EMBEDDING_LR for the shared Adam group. Multiply the logits by a fixed 1/sqrt(model_dim) factor before the softcap so the tied output scale stays stable. Everything else stays the same. This halves the vocab-sized parameters and should free optimizer budget for the transformer blocks.
backlog.title: Tie input embedding and lm_head weights

backlog.spec: Raise TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 and keep every learning rate unchanged. The gradient accumulation count doubles automatically, so DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE stays 64. This tests the opposite direction of the smaller-batch idea: fewer, less noisy steps in the fixed 300 s budget. Check that the step count logged by the script still runs the full time budget.
backlog.title: Larger total batch with the same LR

backlog.spec: In the Muon parameter grouping, put the attention Q, K, V and output projections in one group and the MLP up and down projections in another. Keep the attention group at MATRIX_LR times 0.5 and the MLP group at MATRIX_LR times 1.0. Apply the same weight decay and momentum to both. Only the group construction changes, not the Muon step itself, so the code change stays small.
backlog.title: Separate Muon LR for attention and MLP matrices

backlog.spec: Scale the Muon learning rate for each block by a factor that falls linearly with depth, from 1.0 at the first layer to 0.6 at the last layer. Compute the factor once when building the parameter groups, so each block's matrices form their own group with lr set to MATRIX_LR times the factor. Leave the Adam groups unchanged. Early layers then move more while later layers stay stable under the high LR.
backlog.title: Depth-scaled Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: Pass label_smoothing=0.05 to the cross-entropy loss used during training only. Keep the evaluation loss exactly as it is in the harness-facing code, and do not change the evaluation call. The smoothing target spreads 5 percent of probability mass across the vocabulary, which regularizes the logits. Watch the training loss for scale changes, since the reported number is recomputed by the harness anyway.
backlog.title: Label smoothing on the training cross-entropy

backlog.spec: During training only, skip each transformer block's residual update with probability 0.1 per block per step, leaving the block input as the output for that block. Scale the surviving branch outputs by 1/(1-0.1) so the expectation matches the full network. Disable the drop entirely at evaluation time. This is a form of layer-wise stochastic depth and should add mild regularization without changing the parameter count.
backlog.title: Stochastic residual block drop during training

backlog.spec: Keep the current linear warmdown but add one restart. At 55 percent of the time budget, reset the learning-rate multiplier to 0.5 and decay it linearly back to the FINAL_LR_FRAC floor by the end of the run. Apply the same multiplier to all parameter groups. The restart may escape a sharp region found in the first phase, and the second decay gives a second annealing pass.
backlog.title: Mid-run learning-rate warm restart

backlog.spec: Add a second prediction target that predicts the token two positions ahead. Reuse the existing lm_head on the final hidden states shifted by one extra position, and compute a cross-entropy loss for that target. Add it to the main loss with weight 0.1. Use only the main head at evaluation time, so the evaluation path is unchanged. This adds a denser training signal per forward pass at a small extra compute cost.
backlog.title: Auxiliary multi-token prediction head

backlog.spec: Skip the rotary position embedding for every fourth attention layer, so layers 3 and 7 of the 8-layer model use no positional encoding and rely on the causal mask alone. Keep RoPE on all other layers and leave the head dimension, window pattern and parameter count unchanged. Mixing position-free layers can help length generalization and changes the inductive bias of the attention stack with only a few lines of code.
backlog.title: NoPE layers without rotary embeddings

backlog.spec: Initialize the output projection of each attention block and each MLP block to exactly zero, so every residual branch starts as the identity. Initialize the token embedding with a standard deviation of 0.5 times its current value. Keep the Muon and Adam learning rates unchanged. This is a pure initialization change that can speed early progress when the first few hundred steps matter in a short budget.
backlog.title: Zero-init output projections with smaller embedding init

backlog.spec: In each transformer block, compute attention and the MLP from the same normalized input and add both outputs to the residual stream in one step: x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), using a single shared RMSNorm per block. Keep the existing per-layer scalars, the window pattern, and the ReLU-squared MLP unchanged. This removes one sequential norm and dependency per layer, which may improve throughput within the fixed 300 s budget, and it changes the gradient path enough to be a real test rather than a tweak.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP residual blocks

backlog.spec: Store the normalized token embedding x0 after the first norm. Before each block after the first, replace the residual input with x = a_i * x + b_i * x0, where a_i and b_i are learnable per-layer scalars initialized to 1.0 and 0.1. Add these scalars to the scalar-parameter group that uses SCALAR_LR and no weight decay. This gives every layer direct access to the token identity signal, which is cheap and tends to help small models that are undertrained in a fixed budget.
backlog.title: Learned mixing of the initial embedding into each layer

backlog.spec: Add one learnable scalar gain per attention head, initialized to 1.0, that multiplies the query-key dot product after QK normalization and before the softmax (equivalently, a learnable per-head temperature). Put these gains in the scalar parameter group with SCALAR_LR and no weight decay. Leave RoPE, the window pattern, and the softmax scale otherwise unchanged. This lets each head choose its sharpness during the short run instead of relying on a fixed 1/sqrt(d) scale.
backlog.title: Learnable per-head attention logit gain

backlog.spec: Replace AdamW for the token embedding and lm_head parameters with the Lion update: u = sign(beta1 * m + (1 - beta1) * g), update the parameter by lr * u, then update m = beta2 * m + (1 - beta2) * g, with beta1 = 0.9 and beta2 = 0.99. Keep the existing EMBEDDING_LR and UNEMBEDDING_LR values, but divide both by 3 for the first trial since Lion's sign update has a larger effective step size. Keep Muon for all matrix parameters and AdamW for the scalars unchanged.
backlog.title: Lion optimizer for embedding and lm_head

backlog.spec: After each optimizer step, for every 2D weight matrix handled by Muon, estimate its largest singular value with 3 power-iteration steps on a persistent random vector, and if it exceeds a cap of 2.0 (scaled by sqrt(fan_in / fan_out) for non-square matrices), rescale the matrix so its spectral norm equals the cap. This is a regularizer that bounds the growth of weights during the high-LR phase and may help the warmdown stability without changing the loss. Skip the cap for embedding, lm_head, and scalar parameters.
backlog.title: Spectral-norm cap on Muon matrix weights

backlog.spec: During training only, add uniform noise to the output of the token embedding layer: x = x + U(-s, s) with s = alpha / sqrt(T * d), where T is the sequence length and d is model_dim, and alpha = 5.0. Apply no noise during evaluation, and keep the evaluation path unchanged. This is a parameter-free regularizer that adds input perturbation, which can reduce overfitting to the training shards, although the run is short enough that the benefit may be small.
backlog.title: NEFTune-style noise on token embeddings

backlog.spec: Maintain a running uniform average of the model parameters, starting once elapsed training time passes 80 percent of the TIME budget and updating after every optimizer step. Keep the average in a separate buffer that is not used for gradient updates. At the end of training, copy the averaged weights into the model before the final evaluation call, leaving the evaluation function itself unchanged. The average smooths the noisy final iterates produced by the Muon steps during the decay phase.
backlog.title: Tail averaging of weights over the last 20 percent of training

backlog.spec: Keep the same warmdown start point at 50 percent of the budget, but decay the Muon matrix learning rate only to 0.2 times its peak by the end, while still decaying the Adam groups (embedding, lm_head, scalars) to 0. Implement this by giving each optimizer group its own end multiplier in the LR schedule function, with the Muon floor at 0.2 and the Adam floor at 0.0. Leave all peak learning rates and the warmdown ratio unchanged. The idea is that Muon keeps making useful progress late in training while the Adam-trained parameters settle.
backlog.title: Separate warmdown endpoints for Muon and Adam groups

backlog.spec: Change the model compile call to torch.compile(model, mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', dynamic=False), keeping the same inputs, batch shapes, and everything else unchanged. Autotuning runs during startup, which is not counted against the 300 s training budget, but the total startup plus training must stay under 450 s, so check the startup time in the log. The goal is to get more optimizer steps in the fixed wall-clock budget from faster fused matmul and attention kernels. Do not change any evaluation code.
backlog.title: Compile with max-autotune kernels

backlog.spec: In the training cross-entropy, multiply the per-token loss by a weight w_t that ramps linearly from 0.5 at position 0 to 1.0 at position 32, and is 1.0 for all later positions, then normalize by the sum of the weights so the overall loss scale is unchanged. This reduces the influence of the first few tokens of each row, where the context is nearly empty and the prediction is largely guesswork, and shifts gradient toward positions where the model can use context. Apply this only to the training loss and leave the evaluation metric unchanged.
backlog.title: Position-weighted training loss that downweights row starts

incumbent.description: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2^19 to 2^18 to increase the number of optimizer steps within the fixed wall-clock budget, potentially improving convergence despite reduced gradient accumulation per step.

memo: Incumbent mean_adjusted is 1.0812 over 2 runs. Helped: batch and data changes. Slot 9 (TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^19 to 2^18) gained 0.0230 but carries a tripwire flag, so check it before building on it. Slot 6 (512-token rows) gained 0.0103. Did not help: architecture and optimizer rewrites. Depth 10 was +0.0151, SwiGLU +0.0086, the t+2 auxiliary loss +0.0233, cosine decay +0.0600 and the Muon LR scale change +0.0266. Small schedule and optimizer tweaks (warmup, momentum warmup, weight decay decay, weight averaging) each landed +0.0015 to +0.0032 and were rejected. Slot 11 (warmdown 0.7) was -0.0024, within noise. Slot 2 (FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.1) was -0.0030 but was rejected. Next: audit the tripwire on slot 9, then try batch 2^17. Retest warmdown 0.7 and FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.1 together on top of the new batch size. Keep edits small.
